rows.note: Use this all-purpose locative construction when something is situated on top of something else.

example.english: The book is on top of the table.
example.jyutping: bun2 syu1 hai2 zoeng1 toi4 soeng6 min6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the uppermost part of a thing, such as the top of a tree.

example.english: The top of this tree is very high.
example.jyutping: ni1 fo2 syu6 ge3 deng2 hou2 gou1

rows.note: Use this specifically for a garment worn on the upper body rather than for a surface or position.

example.english: This top still looks new after being washed.
example.traditional: 呢件上衣洗完仲好似新咁。
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 soeng6 ji1 sai2 jyun4 zung6 hou2 ci5 san1 gam3

rows.note: Use this for the best or highest-ranked option in a field, such as a top school.

example.english: They got into a top university.
example.jyutping: keoi5 jap6 zo2 gaan1 ding2 zim1 daai6 hok6

rows.note: Use this for a lid or cap that closes a container.

example.english: The top of the jar is missing.
example.jyutping: go3 zeon1 ge3 koi3 m4 gin3 zo2

rows.note: Use this to praise someone or something as excellent or first-rate, such as a top lawyer.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 leot6 si1 zan1 hai6 jat1 lau4

rows.note: Use this for first place or the highest rank, such as being top of a class.

example.english: I finally came top of the class.
example.traditional: 我終於考到全班第一名。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 jyu1 haau2 dou2 cyun4 baan1 dai6 jat1 ming4
